title.narrative: DocudaysUA International Documentary Human Rights Festival - 2026
DocudaysUA International Documentary Human Rights Festival - 2026

description.narrative:
GOAL: Create a society of free people and strengthen democracy in Ukraine by promoting, educating, and protecting human rights and cultural products for various target groups through "DOCUDAYS" powerful systematic activities and institutional capacity development.
Objective 1: Contribute to shaping civil society in Ukraine by using documentary films for awareness raising activities and human rights protection.
Output objectives: - Enable multistakeholder engagement and platforms for dialogue around documentary films and human rights by holding nationwide and yearlong activities, including Docudays UA festival in Kyiv (June 2024, June 2025, June 2026), DOCU/CLUB Network (yearlong), Travelling Docudays UA festival (every autumn since 2025), DOCUSPACE online cinema (yearlong).
- Preserve the history of the full-scale war, ensure systematic documentation of war crimes and widely communicate about the war in Ukraine via the development of the Ukraine War Archive.
- Increase human rights awareness by holding systematic human rights events and campaigns in the framework of the Docudays UA festival in Kyiv, DOCU/ CLUB Network, and Travelling Docudays UA festival. - Promote Ukrainian culture and spread the truth about the russian invasion of Ukraine to the global community by holding a series of cultural diplomacy events in Europe and beyond. - Enhance the network of Ukrainian film industry professionals within the DOCU/ PRO industry section and hold systematic educational events on documentary films to further develop human rights documentary film production by Ukrainian filmmakers.
Objective 2: To become a more sustainable and effective civil society organization in fulfilling its mission, vision and goal.
Output objectives: - Ensure continuous funding of the organizations activities to enable its sustainable development. - Implement effective strategies, policies, procedures, and operational plans in response to war challenges. - Preserve the team, hire new staff, and systematically train them to meet the strategic goals. - Continue to integrate crosscutting aspects into all areas of the organizations activities. - Increase "DOCUDAYS" visibility among beneficiaries and stakeholders. - Strengthen the capacity of "DOCUDAYS" networks. - Implement and improve M&E systems and integrate principles and tools of results-based management (RBM) for the main "DOCUDAYS" activities to track the organizational performance in implementing the organizations strategy for 20242026.

Decision DocudaysUA International Documentary Human Rights Festival

description.narrative:
In 2025, against the backdrop of continued full-scale war and severe humanitarian pressure, Docudays UAs operations led to meaningful and noticeable changes in how citizens, communities, institutions, and civil society actors engage with human rights, democratic values, and each other.
First, the programme significantly strengthened civic awareness and engagement. Large-scale outreach through festivals, campaigns, and events contributed to enhanced knowledge and attitudes. A majority of participants particularly young and first-time attendees reported a deeper understanding of human rights and protection mechanisms. This reflects a clear transition from passive consumption of content to more active reflection, discussion, and civic engagement.
At the community level, the DOCU/CLUB Network has evolved into a critical infrastructure for local resilience and participation. Across Ukraine, including near-frontline areas, film clubs have become safe and trusted spaces where people not only engage with human rights topics but also come together to address shared challenges, support one another, and interact with local authorities. The rapid expansion of the network speaks favorably of a decentralized, self-sustaining civic engagement, where local actors increasingly take ownership of dialogue and problem-solving processes.
The Ukraine War Archive represents another major outcome, fundamentally changing how evidence of war crimes is collected, preserved, and used. Civil society organizations, media actors, and accountability mechanisms now operate with access to a structured and secure repository of verified information. This has shifted practices from fragmented and ad hoc documentation toward systematic, standardised, and legally relevant evidence gathering, directly contributing to national and international justice efforts. Collaboration has improved, with over 150 actors working through coordinated systems and shared methodologies, replacing isolated efforts. Civil society is increasingly used by government bodies and investigators, evolving from observers into active partners in accountability processes.
The use of advanced technologies (AI, big data) has further enhanced capabilities, enabling large-scale analysis and new functions such as tracing patterns and identifying missing persons.
At the institutional level, relationships between civil society and state actors have also evolved. The formalized cooperation with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs illustrates a growing recognition of civil society as a strategic partner in advancing Ukraines international advocacy and cultural diplomacy. This marks a shift toward more structured and collaborative approaches, where documentary film and human rights narratives are actively used to amplify Ukraines voice globally.
In parallel, the programme has contributed to changing standards within the cultural sector itself. Accessibility measuressuch as subtitles, audio description, and sign language interpretationhave become common practices rather than optional add-ons, broadening inclusion for audiences with different needs. These changes indicate a move toward more responsible, inclusive, and forward-looking cultural practices.
Overall, civil society actors are seemingly now more capable, connected, and vocal, contributing directly to accountability, public discourse, and long-term justice.
Overall, the programme is clearly making a difference. It has strengthened the capacity of citizens to engage with democratic values, enabled communities to act collectively under extreme conditions, enhanced the role of civil society in accountability and advocacy, and fostered more collaborative relationships with public institutions. These outcomes are particularly significant in the Ukrainian context, where resilience, social cohesion, and credible evidence for justice are essential in the face of ongoing war.
